sensesIntro.en: Fireman means a firefighter or a person who tends a furnace fire.
sensesIntro.cn: fireman 意为消防员或司炉工。

core.en: A person whose work is bound to fire.
core.cn: 工作与火紧密相连的人。

branches.en: One who puts out fires.
branches.cn: 扑灭火灾的人。

branches.en: One who keeps a furnace burning.
branches.cn: 让炉火持续燃烧的人。

branches.en: Both work directly with fire.
branches.cn: 两者都直接与火打交道。

branches.en: Danger defines the modern job.
branches.cn: 危险定义了这份现代职业。

branches.en: Machines once needed human fire.
branches.cn: 机器曾需要人来添火。

intro.en: Fireman is a native compound of two Old English words.
intro.cn: fireman 是由两个古英语词构成的本族复合词。

latinIntro.en: English fireman has no Latin ancestor; Latin ignis and homo are only semantic parallels.
latinIntro.cn: 英语 fireman 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 ignis（火）与 homo（人）只是语义对应词。

items.exampleCN: 两名消防员进入了大楼。

items.example: The truck returned to the firehouse.
A man stood at the gate.
The stoker kept the boiler hot.
items.exampleCN: 司炉工让锅炉保持高温。

definition_en: in a way that is correct and free from error
core_image: 报站员一字不差地念出站名和时间
scene: 护士把药量抽到刻度线上，又核对了一遍。 The nurse measured the dose accurately.
sceneCN: 这里的 accurately 是「精确地」（第 2 个义项：测量数值准确）；句意是护士把药量量得很准。

derivatives.zh: 由副词去后缀还原为形容词，义为「准确的」
由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「准确性」
加否定前缀构成，义为「不准确的」

senses.title: Without misstating the facts
senses.definition: in a way that reports the facts correctly
senses.definitionCN: 以符合事实、没有说错的方式
senses.example: She accurately described the man at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 她准确描述了门口那个男人的样子。
senses.why: The adverb keeps the Latin idea of care and applies it to speech: every detail is checked before it is said.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词保留了拉丁语「用心」的意思，并把它用在说话上：每个细节都先核对再说出口。

senses.title: With a precise reading
senses.definition: with numbers or amounts that come very close to the true value
senses.definitionCN: 所用数值或分量非常接近真实值地
senses.example: The device accurately records the room temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 这台设备能精确记录室内温度。
senses.why: Care moves from words to instruments, and the adverb now describes how a needle or a meter lands on the true figure.
senses.whyCN: 「用心」从言语挪到仪器上，这个副词便形容指针或仪表如何落在真实数值上。

senses.title: With a true aim
senses.definition: in a way that sends something to the intended point
senses.definitionCN: 把东西送到预定点上地
senses.example: He threw the ball accurately into the basket.
senses.exampleCN: 他把球精准地投进了篮筐。
senses.why: A target gives care a visible test, so the adverb marks the throw whose line ends exactly where the eye intended.
senses.whyCN: 靶子给「用心」一个看得见的检验，于是这个副词标记出那条终点正合心意的投掷线。

intro.en: The adverb is the Latin care adjective plus the English manner ending.
intro.cn: 这个副词由拉丁语的「用心」形容词加英语方式词尾构成。

items.en: cura meant care and attention.
items.cn: cura 意为关心与留意。

items.en: accuratus described work done with care.
items.cn: accuratus 形容用心做成的活。

items.en: accurate came into English as an adjective of exactness.
items.cn: accurate 作为表示精确的形容词进入英语。

items.en: the ending -ly turned it into an adverb of manner.
items.cn: 词尾 -ly 把它变成方式副词。

items.en: accurately now modifies verbs of describing, measuring and aiming.
items.cn: 如今 accurately 修饰描述、测量与瞄准一类动词。

note.en: The first group is the accurate family; the second is other adverbs of exactness.
note.cn: 第一组是 accurate 词族；第二组是别的表示精确的副词。

entries.definition: in an exact and careful way
in a way that is right
in a way that stays true to the original

normalIntro.en: The adverb is simply accurate plus the manner ending -ly.
normalIntro.cn: 这个副词就是 accurate 加方式词尾 -ly。

normal.en: accurate plus -ly gives the manner of doing something with care.
normal.cn: accurate 加 -ly，得到「用心去做」的方式。

normal.en: the base cura means care, so the adverb never means fast.
normal.cn: 词根 cura 意为用心，所以这个副词从不表示「快」。

normal.en: it pairs naturally with describe, measure, predict and report.
normal.cn: 它天然与 describe、measure、predict、report 搭配。

normal.en: in- on the adjective turns it into its opposite.
normal.cn: 形容词前加 in- 就得到反义。

normal.en: more and most form the comparative and superlative.
normal.cn: 比较级与最高级分别用 more 和 most。

abstract.en: Hear a station announcer reading every name without a slip.
abstract.cn: 想象报站员把每个站名都念得一字不差。

abstract.en: See a nurse lining the syringe up with the mark.
abstract.cn: 想象护士把针筒对准刻度线。

abstract.en: Picture a ball dropping cleanly through the hoop.
abstract.cn: 想象球干干净净地穿过篮筐。

examples.en: The guide accurately described the route up the mountain.
examples.cn: 向导准确描述了上山路线。

examples.en: This watch keeps time accurately even in cold weather.
examples.cn: 这块表在寒冷天气里也走得很准。

examples.en: She accurately predicted the result of the vote.
examples.cn: 她准确预测了投票结果。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克尤瑞特利」——阿克每做一步都回头核对，做事特利落又特准。

root: 由 accurate（拉丁语 accuratus，用心的、精确的）加副词词尾 -ly 构成；核心仍是 cura（关心、留意），表示以用心、无误的方式去做。

sensesIntro.en: The adverb carries one kind of care into three arenas: speech, measurement and aim.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个副词把同一种「用心」带进三个场域：说话、测量与瞄准。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand that checks before it moves.
core.cn: 核心意象：动手之前先核对的那只手。

branches.en: words that match the scene described
branches.cn: 与所述场景相符的言语

branches.en: instruments that stop at the true figure
branches.cn: 停在真实数值上的仪器

branches.en: a throw that ends on the chosen point
branches.cn: 落在选定点上的投掷

branches.en: exactness in both words and numbers
branches.cn: 言语与数字两方面的精确

branches.en: a reading and a shot that both hit true
branches.cn: 读数与投射都正中目标

intro.en: A Latin care stem, an adjective ending and an adverb ending make the word.
intro.cn: 拉丁语「用心」词干、形容词词尾与副词词尾，三者拼成这个词。

latinIntro.en: The care root cura is also behind cure and curator.
latinIntro.cn: 表示「用心」的词根 cura 也藏在 cure 与 curator 后面。

definition_zh: 你自己；你亲自；你的正常状态
definition_en: the reflexive form of you, used when the person spoken to is both the doer and the receiver of an action
core_image: 一个人照镜子，镜里镜外都是他自己
scene: 朋友第一次独自做饭，发来一张焦黑的锅底照片。 You need to be patient while learning the whole routine.
sceneCN: 这里 yourself 是「你自己」（第 1 个义项：反身代词，动作的执行者与承受者是同一个人）；句意为学做饭时要对自己有耐心。一个人照镜子，镜里镜外都是自己，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 你亲自；你本人（强调用法）
你的正常状态；你的常态

derivatives.zh: yourself 的复数形式，义为「你们自己」
yourself 的后一成分，义为「自我；自身」
由 self 加 -ish 构成，义为「自私的」，与 yourself 同一词根

senses.title: The same person as doer and receiver
senses.definition: used when the listener does something to or for the same person, so doer and receiver are one
senses.definitionCN: 听话者对自己做某事或为自己做某事，执行者与承受者合为一人
senses.example: You should give yourself more time to learn the new job.
senses.exampleCN: 你该给自己更多时间熟悉新工作。
senses.why: Self is added to the possessive so the pronoun can point back at its own subject, which is what a reflexive needs.
senses.whyCN: 把 self 加到所有格后，代词才能指回自己的主语，这正是反身代词所需的。

senses.title: The person in emphasis
senses.definition: used after a noun or at the end of a clause to stress that it was really the listener
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词后或句末，强调确实是听话者本人
senses.example: You yourself said the plan would never work.
senses.exampleCN: 你自己说过这个计划行不通。
senses.why: Repeating the pronoun as self makes the reference impossible to miss, so it becomes a way of stressing.
senses.whyCN: 把代词以 self 的形式重说一遍，指谁就绝不含糊，于是成了强调手段。

senses.title: The natural state
senses.definition: used after be or feel to mean one's normal healthy or usual condition
senses.definitionCN: 用在 be 或 feel 之后，指正常、健康或平时的状态
senses.example: You have not been yourself since the move.
senses.exampleCN: 搬家以后你就不太对劲了。
senses.why: If the self is the whole person, then being away from it is being unlike one's normal state.
senses.whyCN: 如果 self 指整个人，那么离开它就是不在平常的状态。

senses.title: The person acting alone
senses.definition: used after by to mean without help from anyone else
senses.definitionCN: 用在 by 之后，表示没有别人帮忙
senses.example: Can you carry both boxes by yourself?
senses.exampleCN: 你一个人能搬这两个箱子吗？
senses.why: Since the reflexive sends the action back to one person, adding by excludes everyone else.
senses.whyCN: 既然反身代词把动作收回到一个人身上，加上 by 就把其他人都排除在外。

senses.title: The person as one of a group
senses.definition: used instead of yourselves when the listener is addressed as one of a group rather than all together
senses.definitionCN: 当听话者代表一群人中的一位、而非整群人一起时，用它代替 yourselves
senses.example: Each of you should introduce yourself before we start.
senses.exampleCN: 开始之前，你们每个人都要介绍一下自己。
senses.why: English divides between one listener and a whole audience inside the same pronoun, so the reflexive has to choose its form.
senses.whyCN: 英语在同一个代词里兼指一个人和整群听众，于是反身形式必须作选择。

intro.en: Yourself joins your, the possessive of you, with self, a word meaning one's own person.
intro.cn: yourself 由 you 的所有格 your 与意为「本人」的 self 组合而成。

items.en: self was an adjective meaning the same or very, and could follow a pronoun to strengthen it.
items.cn: 古英语 self 是形容词，意为「同一的、正是的」，跟在代词后起加强作用。

items.en: Combinations such as þe selfum appear in prose, though the modern shape came later.
items.cn: 古英语散文里已见 þe selfum 之类组合，现代形式则出现较晚。

items.en: The modern pattern of pronoun plus self formed, with yourself and himself among the first.
items.cn: 代词加 self 的现代模式形成，yourself 与 himself 属于最早的一批。

items.en: The reflexive and the emphatic uses settled, and the by yourself pattern became everyday.
items.cn: 反身用法与强调用法固定，by yourself 也成了日常说法。

items.en: The plural yourselves was kept for groups, so the two forms divide the work.
items.cn: 复数 yourselves 保留给群体使用，两种形式就此分工。

note.en: Yourself is compared with the other pronouns ending in -self and with related reflexives.
note.cn: yourself 与其它以 -self 结尾的代词以及相关反身形式作对照。

entries.definition: the reflexive for a group of listeners
the reflexive for a male third person
the reflexive for anyone, in formal style
entries.definitionCN: 正式对等形式，一个人自己

normalIntro.en: The pattern is simple: possessive plus self, and the possessive shows whose self it is.
normalIntro.cn: 模式很简单：所有格加 self，所有格说明是谁的自己。

normal.en: Your is the possessive, so yourself literally marks the self that belongs to you.
normal.cn: your 是所有格，所以 yourself 字面上就是属于你的那个自己。

normal.en: Swap the possessive and the whole set appears: myself, himself, herself, ourselves.
normal.cn: 换掉所有格，整套词就出来了：myself、himself、herself、ourselves。

normal.en: The plural is irregular in its first half but regular in its second: yourselves.
normal.cn: 复数前半不规则，后半规则：yourselves。

normal.en: By yourself means alone, because a reflexive pushes the action back to one person.
normal.cn: by yourself 意为独自，因为反身代词把动作收回一个人身上。

normal.en: Self began as an adjective meaning very, which explains how the pronoun became emphatic.
normal.cn: self 原是意为「正是」的形容词，这解释了代词为何变得强调。

abstract.en: Picture a mirror where the person outside and the person inside are doing the same thing.
abstract.cn: 想象一面镜子，镜外的人和镜里的人做着同一件事。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pointing back at its own chest instead of at someone else.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手不指别人，而是指回自己的胸口。

abstract.en: Picture an empty chair at a family meal where one person has been unlike himself all evening.
abstract.cn: 想象家宴上一张空椅，那个人整晚都不像平时的自己。

examples.en: You should give yourself more time to learn the new job.
examples.cn: 你该给自己更多时间熟悉新工作。

examples.en: You yourself said the plan would never work.
examples.cn: 你自己说过这个计划行不通。

examples.en: Can you carry both boxes by yourself?
examples.cn: 你一个人能搬这两个箱子吗？

dict_mnemonic.text: 「有谁儿媳妇」——照镜子时自问「有谁儿媳妇比我还操心」，镜子里那位就是你自己，于是 yourself 指你自己。

root: your（you 的所有格，古英语 ēower）加 self（古英语 self，意为「本人、正是」），构成反身代词。

sensesIntro.en: A pronoun that points back at its own subject becomes reflexivity, emphasis, a sense of normal state, and a way to say alone.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个指回自身主语的代词，长出了反身、强调、常态与「独自」几种用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mirror that shows the same person twice
core.cn: 核心意象：镜里镜外是同一个人的镜子

branches.en: Sending the action back to the doer is the core use.
branches.cn: 把动作送回执行者，是核心用法。

branches.en: Repeating the reference makes it emphatic.
branches.cn: 把指称再说一遍，就成了强调。

branches.en: Being away from the self means being unlike one's normal state.
branches.cn: 离开自己，就是不在平常的状态。

branches.en: With by, the reflexive shuts everyone else out.
branches.cn: 配上 by，反身代词就把别人都关在门外。

branches.en: Addressed to individuals within a group, the singular form is chosen.
branches.cn: 对群体中逐位说话时，选单数形式。

intro.en: Yourself is a compound of a possessive and self, and the -self family works as a pattern.
intro.cn: yourself 是所有格与 self 的复合词，-self 这一族按同一模式构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin used the pronoun se for the reflexive, and that element survives in English in words such as suicide and separate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用代词 se 表反身，这个成分以 suicide、separate 等词残留在英语中。

items.exampleCN: 他刮胡子时刮伤了自己。

items.example: One should not praise oneself too much.
Latin se appears in secede and seduce.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 se 出现在 secede 与 seduce 中。

definition_zh: 收银员；出纳员；革职；罢免
definition_en: a person who receives and pays out money in a shop or bank, or to dismiss someone from a position of service
core_image: 守在钱箱旁清点钱款的人
scene: 超市收银台前排着长队。 The cashier scanned each item and told her the total.
sceneCN: 这里 cashier 指「收银员」（第 1 个义项：在商店收款的人）；句意是收银员逐件扫码，告诉她总价。

senses.title: A person who handles payments
senses.definition: a person whose job is to take money from customers or to pay money out at a bank
senses.definitionCN: 负责向顾客收款或在银行付钱的工作人员
senses.example: The cashier gave me the wrong change.
senses.exampleCN: 收银员找错了钱。
senses.why: The French source meant the keeper of the money box, so the person is named after the box itself.
senses.whyCN: 法语源词指看管钱箱的人，所以这个人是按那只钱箱来命名的。

senses.title: To dismiss from service
senses.definition: to dismiss an officer or official from a position, usually with disgrace
senses.definitionCN: 把军官或官员免职，通常带有不光彩的意味
senses.example: The colonel was cashiered for neglect of duty.
senses.exampleCN: 那名上校因玩忽职守被革职。
senses.why: This verb comes from a different source meaning to break or discard, and it pictures the box of office being thrown away.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词另有来源，意为打破或丢弃，画面是把职权这只盒子扔掉。

intro.en: The shop sense comes from a French word for the keeper of a money box, while the dismissal sense comes from a separate verb meaning to break or discard.
intro.cn: 商店义来自法语中看管钱箱的人，革职义则来自另一个意为打破或丢弃的动词。

items.en: Capsa, a box, underlies the French words for a money chest and its keeper.
items.cn: 拉丁语 capsa（盒子）是法语中钱柜及其看管者说法的源头。

items.en: Caisse named a money box and caissier the person who kept it.
items.cn: 法语 caisse 指钱箱，caissier 指看管它的人。

items.en: English borrowed cashier for the officer who handled a company's money.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 cashier，指管理公司钱款的职员。

items.en: A separate verb, recorded as casseren or casser, meant to break and then to dismiss.
items.cn: 另有一个动词，记作 casseren 或 casser，本义为打破，后指免职。

items.en: Modern English keeps both strands: the shop worker and the disgraced officer.
items.cn: 现代英语两条线都保留：商店职员与被革职的军官。

note.en: The first group follows the money-box root, the second gathers people who handle money at a counter.
note.cn: 第一组沿钱箱词根展开，第二组收在柜台处理钱款的人。

entries.definition: coins and notes used as money
entries.definitionCN: 作为货币的硬币和纸币

entries.definition: the act of dismissing an officer
a book recording money received and paid
a bank clerk who pays out money
a person who keeps records or serves customers
entries.definitionCN: 管账或接待顾客的职员

entries.definition: the person in charge of a group's money

normalIntro.en: These hooks link cashier to cash, to the -ier ending and to the separate dismissal verb.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把 cashier 与 cash、-ier 词尾以及另一个革职动词联系起来。

normal.en: Cashier is cash plus -ier, the person who deals with the cash all day.
normal.cn: cashier 就是 cash 加 -ier，整天与现金打交道的人。

normal.en: The ending -ier also marks a person in soldier and courier.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ier 在 soldier 和 courier 里同样表示人。

normal.en: Bank cashier and head cashier fix the job sense in two short phrases.
normal.cn: bank cashier 与 head cashier 用两个短搭配固定了职业义。

normal.en: Cashiered is almost always used of officers, which keeps the dismissal sense apart.
normal.cn: cashiered 几乎只用于军官，这使革职义与收银义区分开来。

normal.en: The spelling keeps one s and a double s sound, unlike cash + ier said quickly.
normal.cn: 拼写上只保留一个 s，读音却像两个 s 连在一起。

abstract.en: Picture a tired worker counting notes behind a glass screen.
abstract.cn: 想象一位疲惫的职员在玻璃后面清点钞票。

abstract.en: Picture an officer handing over a sword and a badge.
abstract.cn: 想象一名军官交出佩剑和徽章。

abstract.en: Picture a drawer sliding open with coins stacked in neat rows.
abstract.cn: 想象抽屉滑开，硬币排成整齐的几行。

examples.en: The cashier asked if I needed a bag.
examples.cn: 收银员问我要不要袋子。

examples.en: She worked as a cashier for two years.
examples.cn: 她当了两年收银员。

examples.en: The officer was cashiered after the inquiry.
examples.cn: 调查结束后那名军官被革职。

dict_mnemonic.text: cashier 可以拆成 cash 加 ier：整天守着 cash 的人，就是收银员。

root: 收银义源自法语 caissier（钱箱看管人），再往上可追到拉丁语 capsa（盒）；革职义另有来源，与意为打破、丢弃的动词相关。

sensesIntro.en: One line runs from the money box to the person who guards it, while a second line runs from breaking to dismissing an officer.
sensesIntro.cn: 一条线从钱箱走到看管钱箱的人，另一条线从打破走到把军官免职。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person standing beside the money box.
core.cn: 核心意象：守在钱箱旁边的人。

branches.en: The keeper of the box becomes the shop and bank worker.
branches.cn: 看管钱箱的人成了商店和银行的职员。

branches.en: The separate break-and-discard verb supplies the dismissal sense.
branches.cn: 另一个表示打破丢弃的动词提供了革职义。

branches.en: Everyday phrases such as bank cashier keep the job sense concrete.
branches.cn: bank cashier 这类日常搭配让职业义保持具体。

branches.en: Both strands involve handing something over: money at a counter or a commission in disgrace.
branches.cn: 两条线都涉及交出东西：柜台上交钱，或不光彩地交出职务。

branches.en: The officer sense stays formal and rare, mostly in military writing.
branches.cn: 军官义偏正式且少见，多出现在军事文字中。

intro.en: Cashier takes the -ier person ending and a few compounds; the rest of its family comes from the base cash.
intro.cn: cashier 带 -ier 表人词尾和少量复合词，其余词族成员来自词基 cash。

latinIntro.en: The money sense traces back through French to Latin capsa, a box.
latinIntro.cn: 钱款义经法语上溯到拉丁语 capsa（盒子）。

items.exampleCN: 革职终结了他的军旅生涯。

items.meaning: the counter where money is paid
items.example: Please go to the cashier's desk.
The cashbook was out of date.

latinEntries.example: Capsa lies behind cashier and cash.
latinEntries.exampleCN: capsa 是 cashier 与 cash 的源头。

definition_zh: 邪恶的；恶劣的；淘气的；极好的（口语）
definition_en: morally bad and cruel, and in informal use playfully naughty or even excellent
core_image: 童话里披黑斗篷的巫婆，指尖亮着一点绿火，嘴角歪着笑
scene: 童话书里那个披黑斗篷的人把药水滴进杯子，嘴角一直歪着笑，孩子们都屏住了呼吸。 The wicked queen offered the girl a shining red apple.
sceneCN: 这里 wicked 是「邪恶的」（第 1 个义项：在道德上坏且残忍）；句意为那个邪恶的王后递给女孩一只发亮的红苹果。黑斗篷、绿火与歪着的笑，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: Morally bad
senses.definition: evil in intention or action, deliberately doing harm to others
senses.definitionCN: 在意图或行为上为恶，有意伤害他人
senses.example: The wicked queen offered the girl a shining red apple.
senses.exampleCN: 那个邪恶的王后递给女孩一只发亮的红苹果。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply bad and evil, the moral judgement a community passes on a person.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思就是坏、恶，是群体对一个人做出的道德判断。

senses.title: Cruel in a smaller way
senses.definition: used of words, weather or tricks that are harsh and deliberately unkind
senses.definitionCN: 形容言辞、天气或恶作剧暴烈而存心不善
senses.example: It was a wicked trick to hide his shoes before the race.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛前把他的鞋藏起来，这恶作剧够坏的。
senses.why: The moral word stretched to anything that causes needless pain, not only to people.
senses.whyCN: 这个道德词扩展到一切造成不必要痛苦的事物，不再只指人。

senses.title: Playfully naughty
senses.definition: used of children or humour that is mischievous but not truly bad
senses.definitionCN: 形容孩子或幽默带点顽皮，但并不真的坏
senses.example: She gave me a wicked little smile and said nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 她冲我调皮地笑了笑，什么也没说。
senses.why: With a child or a joke the danger is only pretended, so the harsh word turns affectionate.
senses.whyCN: 用在孩子或玩笑上时，危险只是假装出来的，严厉的词于是变得亲昵。

senses.title: Excellent, in slang
senses.definition: in modern informal speech, used to praise something as very good or impressive
senses.definitionCN: 在现代口语中，用来称赞某事极好、令人赞叹
senses.example: He plays a wicked guitar solo in the last verse.
senses.exampleCN: 他在最后一段弹了一段绝妙的吉他独奏。
senses.why: Slang often flips a bad word into praise, because the intensity of the judgement stays and only its sign changes.
senses.whyCN: 俚语常把贬词翻成褒词，因为判断的强度仍在，只是方向反了。

intro.en: Wicked comes from Middle English wikked, from wicke, meaning evil or bewitched, which is linked to wicca, a witch.
intro.cn: wicked 来自中古英语 wikked，源头 wicke 意为「邪恶的、被施了妖术的」，与 wicca（女巫）相关。

items.en: The root wicce meant a female magician, and the related adjective carried the sense of bewitched.
items.cn: 词根 wicce 指女巫，相关形容词带有「被施了妖术」之意。

items.en: Wikked described a person who was evil or given to the dark arts, and the -ed ending marked the adjective.
items.cn: wikked 描述行恶或习于邪术的人，-ed 词尾标示形容词。

items.en: The ending lost its separate force, and the word became the plain adjective for moral evil.
items.cn: 该词尾失去了独立作用，这个词成为表示道德恶的普通形容词。

items.en: With children and jokes it softened into playful naughtiness, as in a wicked grin.
items.cn: 用在孩子和玩笑上时，它软化为顽皮的淘气，如 a wicked grin。

items.en: Modern slang turned it into high praise, so a wicked solo is a fine one.
items.cn: 现代俚语把它变成高度称赞，所以 a wicked solo 指的是一段漂亮独奏。

note.en: The first group gathers witch-family words that look or sound similar, the second the words for evil and for mischief.
note.cn: 第一组收与 witch 同族或形近的词，第二组收表示邪恶与淘气的词。

entries.definition: A woman said to work magic, behind the old adjective.
The string in a candle that feeds the flame.
Woven from thin branches, quite unrelated.
Morally bad in a deep and serious way.
Willing to cause pain without pity.
Bad in a small and childish way.

normalIntro.en: Wicked carries the old word for a witch, so the fairy-tale picture is the shortest road into it.
normalIntro.cn: wicked 里藏着古老的「女巫」一词，所以童话画面是通往它最近的路。

normal.en: Witch hides inside wicked; a witch was once called wicce.
normal.cn: wicked 里藏着 witch，而女巫曾被叫作 wicce。

normal.en: The -ed only made it an adjective, like crooked from crook.
normal.cn: 这个 -ed 只是把它变成形容词，像 crooked 来自 crook。

normal.en: A wicked stepmother and a wicked smile differ only in how dangerous they are.
normal.cn: 恶毒的后母与调皮的一笑，区别只在于危险程度。

normal.en: Modern slang flips it: a wicked solo is great, not evil.
normal.cn: 现代俚语把它翻转：a wicked solo 是好，不是坏。

normal.en: No peace for the wicked is a joke said while working late.
normal.cn: no peace for the wicked 是加班时的自嘲。

abstract.en: See a black cloak and one hand raised in the dark.
abstract.cn: 看见一件黑斗篷和黑暗中举起的一只手。

abstract.en: Feel the room go quiet when a certain smile appears.
abstract.cn: 感觉某个笑容一出现，房间里就安静下来。

abstract.en: Hear laughter that is too pleased with itself.
abstract.cn: 听见一阵对自己太满意的笑。

examples.en: In the story a wicked giant guards the bridge.
examples.cn: 故事里有个邪恶的巨人守着那座桥。

examples.en: That was a wicked thing to say to your brother.
examples.cn: 对弟弟说那种话可真恶毒。

examples.en: She has a wicked sense of humour that keeps us laughing.
examples.cn: 她的幽默感刁钻得很，总让我们发笑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「维克的」——维克这个人在故事里总干坏事，所以是邪恶的。

root: 古英语 wicce（女巫）→ 中古英语 wicke（邪恶）→ wikked → 现代英语 wicked；同族有 witch、wickedness、wickedly。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins as a moral judgement tied to witchcraft, widens to harsh words and weather, softens towards a child s mischief, and in slang flips into praise.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词最初是与巫术相关的道德判断，扩展到严厉的言辞与天气，再软化为孩子的顽皮，最后在俚语中翻成称赞。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a black cloak, green fire on a fingertip, a crooked smile.
core.cn: 核心意象：黑斗篷、指尖的绿火与歪着的笑。

branches.en: The fairy-tale branch: the queen and the red apple.
branches.cn: 童话分支：王后与那只红苹果。

branches.en: The trick branch: shoes hidden before a race.
branches.cn: 恶作剧分支：赛前被藏起来的鞋。

branches.en: The affection branch: a small, wicked smile.
branches.cn: 亲昵分支：调皮的一笑。

branches.en: The praise branch: a wicked guitar solo.
branches.cn: 称赞分支：一段绝妙的吉他独奏。

branches.en: The judgement branch: a verdict on a person or a deed.
branches.cn: 评判分支：对人或行为的裁决。

intro.en: Wicked is an old adjective formed with the ending -ed on a stem meaning evil, and it now builds adverbs and nouns with -ly and -ness.
intro.cn: wicked 是在表示邪恶的词干上加 -ed 构成的古老形容词，现在还可用 -ly、-ness 派生副词与名词。

latinIntro.en: The word is native Germanic and has no Latin ancestor; the Latin entries below show the borrowed words that translate it.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是本土日耳曼语，没有拉丁语祖先；下面的拉丁条目给出用来翻译它的借入词。

items.example: It turned the old noun into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它把古老的名词变成形容词。

items.example: It is the oldest shape behind the word.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个词背后最古老的形态。

items.example: It kept the stem without the ending.
items.exampleCN: 它保留了没有词尾的词干。

items.example: A separate word from the same family sound.
items.exampleCN: 同族中一个形似的独立词。

items.meaning: the cruel figure of fairy tales
items.example: The fixed frame of the old sense.

latinEntries.example: It gives English malice and malignant.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它给出英语的 malice 与 malignant。

definition_en: to make a loud deep sound, or such a sound itself
core_image: 夜色中昂首长吼的狮子
scene: 狮子在夜色中发出一声长吼，声音传得很远。 The lion's roar carried far into the night.
sceneCN: 这里 roar 是「吼声」（第 1 个义项：动物发出的低沉巨响）；句意：狮子在夜色中发出一声长吼，声音传得很远。

senses.title: An animal's deep cry
senses.definition: a long loud sound made by a large animal
senses.definitionCN: 大型动物发出的长而响的声音
senses.example: We heard a lion roar across the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 我们听见狮子在山谷对面吼叫。
senses.why: The deep open sound belongs first to big animals.
senses.whyCN: 这种深沉开阔的声音首先属于大型动物。

senses.title: A human shout
senses.definition: to shout in a very loud voice
senses.definitionCN: 用极大的声音喊叫
senses.example: He roared at the driver to stop.
senses.exampleCN: 他朝司机大吼让车停下。
senses.why: Anger or excitement makes the voice animal-loud.
senses.whyCN: 愤怒或激动会让人的声音大得像野兽。

senses.title: A loud engine sound
senses.definition: a loud continuous noise, as of engines or traffic
senses.definitionCN: 发动机或车流等发出的持续巨响
senses.example: The roar of the truck shook the windows.
senses.exampleCN: 卡车的轰鸣震动了窗户。
senses.why: Machines can sound like a beast in the dark.
senses.whyCN: 机器在黑暗中听起来像一头野兽。

intro.en: Roar comes from Old English rārian, to roar like a beast.
intro.cn: roar 源自古英语 rārian，意为像野兽般吼叫。

items.en: Rārian means to roar.
items.cn: rārian 意为吼叫。

items.en: The sound stays tied to lions and beasts.
items.cn: 这个声音一直与狮子和野兽相连。

items.en: People and crowds begin to roar too.
items.cn: 人和人群也开始「吼叫」。

items.en: Engines and traffic roar in cities.
items.cn: 城市里发动机与车流轰鸣。

items.en: Roar with laughter becomes a set phrase.
items.cn: roar with laughter 成为固定短语。

note.en: Roar is deep and long; shout is human and shorter.
note.cn: roar 低沉悠长，shout 是人的较短喊声。

entries.definition: to shout in a deep voice
to make a loud rolling sound

normalIntro.en: Roar is the sound that fills a whole valley.
normalIntro.cn: roar 是能填满整个山谷的声音。

normal.en: A lion roars across the dark plain.
normal.cn: a lion roars 狮子在黑暗平原上吼叫。

normal.en: Roar with laughter means laugh very loudly.
normal.cn: roar with laughter 意为放声大笑。

normal.en: The crowd's roar filled the stadium.
normal.cn: the roar of the crowd 填满体育场。

normal.en: To roar at someone is to shout angrily.
normal.cn: roar at 某人是愤怒地吼叫。

normal.en: A truck can roar past a quiet house.
normal.cn: 卡车会轰鸣着驶过安静的房屋。

abstract.en: Picture a lion's breath in cold night air.
abstract.cn: 想象寒夜里狮子的吐息。

abstract.en: Imagine a wave of sound hitting a stone wall.
abstract.cn: 想象声浪撞上石墙。

abstract.en: Think of engines growling like distant beasts.
abstract.cn: 想象引擎像远处野兽般低吼。

examples.en: The wind roared through the trees.
examples.cn: 风穿过树林呼啸。

examples.en: The audience roared with approval.
examples.cn: 观众大声叫好。

examples.en: We could not hear over the roar of the water.
examples.cn: 水声轰鸣，我们听不清。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「roar」听起来像「吼儿」——张开嘴吼出来的声音，就是咆哮。

root: 古英语 rārian（吼叫）→ roar，核心义「低沉、长久、充满空间的声音」，从兽吼扩展到人声与机器。

sensesIntro.en: Roar means a beast's deep cry, a human shout, or a loud machine noise.
sensesIntro.cn: roar 指野兽的低吼、人的大喊，或机器的轰鸣。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sound filling a whole valley.
core.cn: 核心意象：填满整个山谷的声音。

branches.en: The beast cry is the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 兽吼是最古老的义项。

branches.en: Angry people borrow the beast sound.
branches.cn: 愤怒的人借用了野兽的声音。

branches.en: Engines take the same deep noise.
branches.cn: 引擎也发出同样的低沉巨响。

branches.en: Beast and human both fill the air with sound.
branches.cn: 野兽与人都会用声音充满空气。

branches.en: Machines in the dark sound like animals.
branches.cn: 黑暗中的机器听起来像动物。

intro.en: Roar is a native English verb from Old English rārian.
intro.cn: roar 是源自古英语 rārian 的英语本族动词。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic, with no Latin prefix.
latinIntro.cn: 该词属于日耳曼语，没有拉丁前缀。

items.example: The phrase widens the sound to joy.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语把声音扩展到欢乐。

definition_zh: 故意的；从容的；仔细考虑
definition_en: done on purpose after thinking; slow and calm; also to think something over carefully
core_image: 一双手把两样东西放在天平两端慢慢比较
scene: 十二个人在屋里坐了很久，桌上的纸翻了又翻，谁也没有先开口。 The jury deliberated for three hours.
sceneCN: 这里 deliberate 指「仔细考虑」（第 3 个义项：反复权衡后作出判断）；句意是陪审团商议了三个小时。

senses.title: Done on purpose
senses.definition: planned and intended rather than accidental
senses.definitionCN: 有计划有意图的，而非偶然发生的
senses.example: The mistake was not deliberate.
senses.exampleCN: 这个错误不是故意的。
senses.why: What is weighed before it is done leaves a mark of choice.
senses.whyCN: 做之前先称量过的事，会留下选择的痕迹。

senses.title: Slow and unhurried
senses.definition: moving or speaking slowly and in a calm, steady way
senses.definitionCN: 动作或说话缓慢、平稳而不慌
senses.example: He crossed the room with deliberate steps.
senses.exampleCN: 他以不慌不忙的脚步穿过房间。
senses.why: A person who is thinking does not want to arrive too soon.
senses.whyCN: 正在思考的人，不想太早到达。

senses.title: Weigh a matter in council
senses.definition: to discuss and think about a question carefully before deciding
senses.definitionCN: 在决定前就一个问题仔细讨论与思考
senses.example: The jury deliberated for three hours.
senses.exampleCN: 陪审团商议了三个小时。
senses.why: Two sides of a question are two pans that must be let settle.
senses.whyCN: 一个问题有两面，就像天平的两个盘，要让它慢慢稳下来。

intro.en: Deliberate comes from Latin deliberare, to weigh well, from de- and libra, a balance.
intro.cn: deliberate 来自拉丁语 deliberare（好好称量），由 de- 与 libra（天平）组成。

items.en: Libra was the scale on which goods were weighed.
items.cn: libra 是称货用的天平。

items.en: Deliberare meant to hold a question in the balance.
items.cn: deliberare 意为把一个问题放到天平上称。

items.en: English took the verb for thinking a matter over.
items.cn: 英语借来这个动词，表示反复思量一件事。

items.en: The adjective added the sense of a calm, slow manner.
items.cn: 形容词用法又添了从容、缓慢的意味。

items.en: Today a deliberate act is one nobody can call careless.
items.cn: 如今一个故意的行为，就是谁也不能说它粗心。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the deli- opening, and the meaning group moves from intended to unhurried.
note.cn: 形近组共用 deli- 开头，近义组则从有意一路走到不慌不忙。

entries.definition: a person sent to act for a group
done because one means to do it

entries.definitionCN: 在发生之前就已想好的

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with two pans of a balance and end with steps that never hurry.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从天平的两个盘开始，落到从不着急的脚步。

normal.en: A choice that was weighed has a different weight in the hand.
normal.cn: 称过的选择，拿在手里的分量不一样。

normal.en: A slow walk across a room says more than a quick word.
normal.cn: 慢慢走过一间屋子，比一句快话更能说明问题。

normal.en: Twelve people in one room are twelve balances, all waiting.
normal.cn: 一屋十二个人，就是十二架天平，一起等着。

normal.en: An accident leaves no plan behind; a deliberate act does.
normal.cn: 意外不留计划，故意的行为会留下。

normal.en: Libra is a balance, so to deliberate is to let the pans settle.
normal.cn: libra 是天平，所以商议就是让两个盘慢慢稳下来。

abstract.en: Picture a hand holding a scale perfectly level.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把天平端得平平的。

abstract.en: Picture a foot placed down heel first, then toe.
abstract.cn: 想象一只脚先落脚跟，再落脚尖。

abstract.en: Picture a circle of chairs and one sheet of paper moving between them.
abstract.cn: 想象一圈椅子，一张纸在中间传来传去。

examples.en: The jury deliberated for three hours.
examples.cn: 陪审团商议了三个小时。

examples.en: The mistake was not deliberate.
examples.cn: 这个错误不是故意的。

examples.en: He crossed the room with deliberate steps.
examples.cn: 他以不慌不忙的脚步穿过房间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 deliberate 记成「地里拨来拨去」：先掂量再动手，就是反复考虑；掂量过的举动，就是故意的。

root: 源自拉丁语 deliberare，词根 libra 是称货用的天平，本义是把一个问题放到天平上称一称。称量要慢，所以它既指「反复考虑」，也指考虑过后有意的举动，还引申出不慌不忙的姿态。

sensesIntro.en: From a question held in a balance, to a choice made with open eyes, to a walk that refuses to hurry.
sensesIntro.cn: 从放在天平上的问题，到睁着眼作出的选择，再到不肯着急的脚步。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two pans of a balance slowly coming level.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平的两个盘慢慢平下来。

branches.en: The first sense is an act that came out of a choice.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是从选择里长出来的行为。

branches.en: The second sense keeps the slow pace of weighing.
branches.cn: 第二个义项保留了称量时那种慢。

branches.en: The third sense is the weighing itself, done aloud in a group.
branches.cn: 第三个义项就是称量本身，在一群人里说出来。

branches.en: A purpose and a discussion are the two ends of one process.
branches.cn: 目的与商议，是同一个过程的两头。

branches.en: Both senses treat time as something worth spending.
branches.cn: 两个义项都把时间当成值得花的东西。

intro.en: Deliberate has a family of adverbs and nouns about thinking before acting.
intro.cn: deliberate 有一族副词与名词，都与「先想再做」有关。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is libra, a balance, with de- giving a sense of thoroughness.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 libra（天平），前缀 de- 带来彻底的意味。

items.example: She deliberately left the door open.

items.exampleCN: 商议很久之后他们同意了。

items.example: The council is a deliberative body.
items.exampleCN: 这个委员会是审议机构。

items.example: The deliberateness of the act was clear.
items.exampleCN: 这个行为的有意十分明显。
他们就这个计划进行了商议。

items.example: The work went on at deliberate speed.
items.exampleCN: 工作以从容的速度推进。

items.example: It was a deliberate attempt to mislead.

definition_en: a broad piece of armour held for defence, something that protects, or to protect someone or something
core_image: 骑士举起一面宽大的木盾挡在身前
scene: 骑士举起了他的盾牌。 The knight raised his shield.
sceneCN: 这里 shield 是「盾牌」（第 1 个义项）；句意：骑士举起了他的盾牌。

senses.title: Defensive board
senses.definition: a wide piece of metal or wood carried to stop blows
senses.definitionCN: 用来挡住击打的宽大金属板或木板
senses.example: The soldier hid behind his shield.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵躲在盾牌后面。
senses.why: This is the oldest and most concrete sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老也最具体的义项。

senses.title: Protection
senses.definition: a person or thing that gives protection
senses.definitionCN: 提供保护的人或事物
senses.example: A tax shield saved the company money.
senses.exampleCN: 一项税收保护让公司省了钱。
senses.why: The board becomes any kind of barrier.
senses.whyCN: 盾牌引申为任何一种屏障。

senses.title: To protect
senses.definition: to protect someone or something from harm
senses.definitionCN: 保护某人或某物免受伤害
senses.example: Parents shield children from danger.
senses.exampleCN: 父母保护孩子远离危险。
senses.why: The noun turns into an action.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为动作。

senses.title: To block
senses.definition: to hold something in front to stop light or view
senses.definitionCN: 把某物挡在前面以遮住光或视线
senses.example: She shielded her eyes from the sun.
senses.exampleCN: 她用手遮挡阳光。
senses.why: Protection narrows to blocking sight.
senses.whyCN: 保护义缩小为遮挡视线。

intro.en: Shield comes from an Old English word for a broad board carried in battle.
intro.cn: shield 来自古英语中表示战场上携带的宽板。

items.en: Scield meant a broad board carried for defence.
items.cn: scield 指战斗中携带的宽大防御板。

items.en: Skjoldr had the same shape and meaning.
items.cn: skjoldr 形状与含义都相同。

items.en: Sheld named both a guard in battle and a heraldic field.
items.cn: sheld 既指战阵中的护具，也指纹章上的盾形。

items.en: Shield extended to police barriers and protective covers.
items.cn: shield 扩展到防暴屏障与防护罩。

items.en: Shield became a verb meaning to protect.
items.cn: shield 成为表示保护的动词。

note.en: Shield is compared with similar-looking words and with words for protection.
note.cn: 把 shield 与形近词以及表示保护的词作比较。

entries.definition: a flat board for holding things
to keep someone safe from harm
to fight to keep something safe

normalIntro.en: A shield is a wall you carry: it stands between you and the blow.
normalIntro.cn: shield 是一堵随身携带的墙：挡在人和击打之间。

normal.en: The knight raised his shield.

normal.en: A shield blocks the blow.

normal.en: The police carried riot shields.

abstract.en: A shield is a wall you carry.

abstract.en: Protection often stands between two people.

dict_mnemonic.text: shield 与古英语 scield 同源，核心画面是「挡在身前的宽板」。

root: 源自原始日耳曼语 skelduz，核心义「宽大的防护板」。

sensesIntro.en: Shield means a defensive board, a protection, to protect, or to block.
sensesIntro.cn: shield 意为盾牌、保护物、保护或遮挡。

core.en: A broad board held between you and harm.
core.cn: 挡在人与伤害之间的一块宽板。

branches.en: The board carried in battle.
branches.cn: 战场上携带的盾板。

branches.en: Anything that stands as protection.
branches.cn: 任何起保护作用的屏障。

branches.en: The act of protecting someone.
branches.cn: 保护某人的动作。

branches.en: A hand held up against light.
branches.cn: 举起手遮挡光线。

branches.en: The object and the action share one word.
branches.cn: 物件与动作共用一个词。

intro.en: Shield forms a small family of protection words.
intro.cn: shield 形成一个表示保护的小词族。

latinIntro.en: Shield has no Latin ancestor; Latin scutum, a shield, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: shield 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 scutum（盾牌）只是语义对应词。

items.example: The shield was made of oak.
The wall provides shielding from noise.
items.exampleCN: 这堵墙起到隔音屏蔽作用。

items.example: He acted as a shielder for the team.

items.exampleCN: 没有盾牌的士兵向前迈步。

items.example: The leaf is broad and shieldlike.

definition_en: the natural light that comes from the sun
core_image: 清晨的光柱穿过窗帘，照在地板上
scene: 早晨房间里洒满阳光。 The room is full of sunlight in the morning.
sceneCN: 这里 sunlight 是「日光、阳光」（第 1 个义项）；句意：早晨房间里洒满阳光。

senses.title: Natural daylight
senses.definition: the natural light of the sun
senses.definitionCN: 太阳发出的自然光
senses.example: The room is full of sunlight in the morning.
senses.exampleCN: 早晨房间里洒满阳光。
senses.why: This is the central everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心的日常义项。

senses.title: Exposure to the sun
senses.definition: the condition of being exposed to the sun
senses.definitionCN: 暴露在阳光下的状态
senses.example: The plant needs plenty of sunlight.
senses.exampleCN: 这种植物需要充足的日照。
senses.why: Here the word counts the light a thing receives.
senses.whyCN: 这里指某物获得的日照量。

intro.en: Sunlight is a compound of sun and light.
intro.cn: sunlight 由 sun（太阳）与 light（光）复合而成。

items.en: Sunne meant the sun.
items.cn: sunne 意为太阳。

items.en: Leoht meant light.
items.cn: leoht 意为光。

items.en: Sunne and light were often paired.
items.cn: sunne 与 light 常被放在一起使用。

items.en: Sunlight named the light of the sun.
items.cn: sunlight 指太阳的光。

items.en: It also meant exposure to that light.
items.cn: 它也指接受这种光的照射。

note.en: Sunlight is compared with look-alike words and with other words for natural light.
note.cn: 把 sunlight 与形近词以及其他表示自然光的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Sunlight is the sun's light arriving on earth.
normalIntro.cn: sunlight 就是太阳的光到达地面。

normal.en: The room is full of sunlight in the morning.
normal.cn: 早晨房间里洒满阳光。

normal.en: The plant needs plenty of sunlight.
normal.cn: 这种植物需要充足的日照。

normal.en: Keep the painting out of direct sunlight.
normal.cn: 别让画受到阳光直射。

normal.en: Sunlight came through the kitchen window.
normal.cn: 阳光从厨房窗户照进来。

normal.en: A cat slept in a pool of sunlight.
normal.cn: 一只猫睡在一片阳光里。

abstract.en: Sunlight is warmth you can see.
abstract.cn: 阳光，是看得见的温暖。

abstract.en: The same sunlight reaches a palace and a field.
abstract.cn: 同样的阳光照着宫殿，也照着田野。

abstract.en: Nothing grows without turning toward some light.
abstract.cn: 没有东西能在不朝向光的情况下生长。

examples.en: The room is full of sunlight in the morning.

examples.en: The plant needs plenty of sunlight.
examples.cn: 这种植物需要充足的日照。

examples.en: Keep the painting out of direct sunlight.
examples.cn: 别让画受到阳光直射。

dict_mnemonic.text: sunlight 由 sun（太阳）与 light（光）复合而成，指日光；direct sunlight 是直射阳光，sunlight exposure 是阳光照射。

root: 由 sun（太阳）与 light（光）复合而成，字面就是太阳的光。

sensesIntro.en: Sunlight means the natural light of the sun, or the amount of it a thing receives.
sensesIntro.cn: sunlight 表示太阳的自然光，也可指某物接受到的日照量。

core.en: The sun's light reaching the ground.
core.cn: 到达地面的太阳光。

branches.en: The room is full of sunlight in the morning.

branches.en: Keep the painting out of direct sunlight.

intro.en: Sunlight combines sun and light, and sun builds many compounds.
intro.cn: sunlight 由 sun 与 light 组合而成，sun 还能构成许多复合词。

latinIntro.en: Both parts are Germanic: sunne and leoht.
latinIntro.cn: 两个部分都属日耳曼语：sunne 与 leoht。

items.example: A sunlit garden opened before us.
items.exampleCN: 一个阳光照耀的花园展现在眼前。

items.example: He got sunburn at the beach.

latinEntries.example: Sunne is the Old English source of sun.

definition_en: a feeling of fondness or tender attachment, or in psychology, feeling as opposed to thought
core_image: 母亲把孩子画的第一张画小心收进抽屉，指尖在纸上停了一下
scene: 老照片摊在桌上，祖母一张张慢慢摩挲。 She looked at the old photographs with great affection.
sceneCN: 这里的 affection 是「喜爱之情」（第 1 个义项：对人、事物温和深厚的爱意）；句意是她满怀深情地看着那些旧照片。

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词后缀 -ion 还原为动词，义为「影响；感动」
加 -ate 构成，义为「充满深情的；亲昵的」
加 -ly 构成，义为「深情地」
由动词过去分词转作形容词，义为「受影响的；做作的」

senses.title: A feeling of fondness
senses.definition: a gentle feeling of liking or caring for a person, animal, or thing
senses.definitionCN: 对人、动物或事物温和的喜欢与关心
senses.example: She looked at the old photographs with great affection.
senses.exampleCN: 她满怀深情地看着那些旧照片。
senses.why: Latin affectio named a state of being moved; when what moves you is a person, the state settles into fondness.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 affectio 指「被触动」的状态；当触动你的是一个人时，这种状态就沉淀为喜爱。

senses.title: Feeling as a mental faculty
senses.definition: in psychology, the emotional side of mental life as distinct from cognition
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中与认知相对的心灵的情感方面
senses.example: The study separates affection from rational judgment.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究把情感与理性判断分开。
senses.why: The technical sense keeps the Latin noun's neutral meaning: any state of being moved, without the warmth of the everyday word.
senses.whyCN: 这个专业义项保留了拉丁名词的中性含义：任何被触动的状态，不带日常用语的温度。

intro.en: A Latin noun for being moved, narrowed in English from any state of feeling to warm liking.
intro.cn: 一个表示「被触动」的拉丁名词，在英语里从任何情感状态收窄为温暖的喜爱。

items.en: facere meant to do or make, the base of fact, effect and the verb afficere.
items.cn: facere 意为「做、造」，是 fact、effect 与动词 afficere 的底子。

items.en: ad 'to' plus facere 'do' formed afficere, to do something to a person, to move or affect them.
items.cn: ad（向）加 facere（做）构成 afficere，意为对某人施加作用、使其动情。

items.en: affectio named the state produced by such action, a disposition or feeling of the mind.
items.cn: affectio 指这种作用产生的状态，即心境或情感。

items.en: Old French affection carried the noun into English with the sense of a settled feeling towards someone.
items.cn: 古法语 affection 把这个名词带入英语，指对某人稳定的情感。

items.en: Everyday English narrowed the word to fondness, while psychology kept the neutral sense of feeling.
items.cn: 日常英语把这个词收窄为「喜爱」，心理学则保留了中性的「情感」义。

note.en: The first group is the affect family; the second gathers words for warm attachment.
note.cn: 第一组是 affect 词族；第二组收表示「温暖依恋」的词。

entries.definition: a gentle liking for someone or something
a much stronger feeling of deep attachment
entries.definitionCN: 爱；程度比 affection 更强

entries.definition: a bond of affection that ties one to another

normalIntro.en: The noun is affect plus -ion: the state of being moved by someone.
normalIntro.cn: 这个名词是 affect 加 -ion：被人触动的状态。

normal.en: affection is the noun built on the verb affect, plus -ion.
normal.cn: affection 是在动词 affect 上加 -ion 构成的名词。

normal.en: The common pattern is affection for a person or place.
normal.cn: 常见搭配是 affection for 一个人或一个地方。

normal.en: Affectionate is the adjective for someone who shows affection easily.
normal.cn: affectionate 形容一个人很容易流露喜爱。

normal.en: In psychology, affection means feeling rather than thought.
normal.cn: 在心理学里，affection 指情感而非思维。

normal.en: Spell the ending -ction, like action and connection.
normal.cn: 词尾拼作 -ction，与 action、connection 一样。

abstract.en: Picture a hand smoothing a child's drawing before it goes into a drawer.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把孩子的画抚平，再收进抽屉。

abstract.en: See the same warmth become a laboratory term for any feeling at all.
abstract.cn: 想象同样的温度变成实验室里指一切情感的术语。

abstract.en: Imagine a bond thin as thread but strong enough to hold a memory.
abstract.cn: 想象一根细如线的纽带，却足以拉住一段记忆。

examples.en: He speaks of his old school with real affection.
examples.cn: 他说起母校时带着真切的感情。

examples.en: The child showed affection by holding her hand.
examples.cn: 孩子拉着她的手来表达亲昵。

examples.en: Psychologists often contrast affection with reasoning.
examples.cn: 心理学家常把情感与推理相对照。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿费克伸」——阿费一伸手，就把那份喜爱递到人心里。

root: 拉丁语 affectio「被触动的状态」来自 afficere（ad- 加 facere「做」，意为对……施加作用）；经古法语 affection 进入英语，日常义收窄为「喜爱」，心理学仍用其中性的「情感」义。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses keep the same state of being moved: everyday warmth towards someone, and the neutral technical name for feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都保留「被触动」这一状态：日常里对人的温暖，以及专业上对情感的中性称呼。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand smoothing a child's drawing before it is put away.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把孩子的画抚平收好。

branches.cn: 祖母摩挲旧照片

branches.en: a child holding a hand to show liking
branches.cn: 孩子拉手表示亲昵

branches.en: fondness for a school one has left
branches.cn: 对已离开的学校的眷恋

branches.en: a study separating feeling from reasoning
branches.cn: 把情感与推理分开的研究

branches.cn: 同一种被触动，生活里温暖，科学里中性
